content:
Do you get the show remote images banner on those emails. It is a yellow band across the top of the email display with options

Another possible issue is the remote links are to scripts, not images. Thunderbird will fetch remote images but not run remote scripts. They are a big security risk. Traditionally it was just twitter and facebook that tended to use tracking scripts to display images but it is becoming more widespread. If you could post the L:ink that is in the source of the mail for one of those images we might stand a chance of determining if that is the issue.

A Third option is your antivirus is blocking remote images either because of the scripts, or because of the number of hits on the same server that occur when you open the email (an attempt to block an unknown distributed denial of service attack at the source.)

content:
This works if followed carefully: Here is the link for moving a profile in Windows when installed in default location: 

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/moving-thunderbird-data-to-a-new-computer

here is the info in brief steps:

  1. ensure thunderbird is NOT running on old machine
  2. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  3. this should open windows file explorer in Appdata\roaming folder
  4. highlight the Thunderbird folder and copy to external media
  5. ensure thunderbird is installed on second computer, started once and NOT running
  6. enter %appdata% in search window on task bar and press Enter key
  7. you should be in Appdata\roaming folder , copy&paste the exported Thunderbird folder there. This may prompt to overwrite an existing folder of same name. allow it
  8. start thunderbird and all should be there

content: My inference is that you want to locate the folders in windows file explorer, not in thunderbird. Do this: - click help>troubleshootinginformation - scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder' - click the 'Mail' folder, as that is where all POP accounts are - you will see names of the POP accounts here, to see message folders for an account, click the desired account folder. You will not see individual messages, as messages are stored in mbox format. You may see such as inbox, inbox.msf, sent, sent.msf. The files named inbox and sent are mbox files that contain the messages. the msf files are indexes into the respective file.
